question:
(i) Why do different spectral series of hydrogen atom have different final energy levels?
(ii) Identify the series for transitions ending at $n_f=3$.

options.A:
(i) Different series occur because all transitions have the same final energy level.
(ii) $n_f=3$ gives the Balmer series.
options.B:
(i) Series are classified by the initial energy level only.
(ii) $n_f=3$ gives the Lyman series.
options.C:
(i) Each series consists of transitions from various higher levels to a fixed final level. Different final levels give different energy differences and hence different spectral series.
(ii) Transitions ending at $n_f=3$ form the Paschen series.
options.D:
(i) Hydrogen has only one spectral series.
(ii) $n_f=3$ gives the ultraviolet Lyman series.
